This report compares the fitted Down syndrome (DS) and typically developing (TD) samples. It pairs draws from separately fitted posteriors to calculate differences and ratios. This assumes independent population-specific parameter distributions; separate datasets alone would not imply independence under every possible joint model. The resulting intervals are Monte Carlo estimates and retain the assumptions and limitations of both fits.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


def _nearest(df, col, val):
    df = df.dropna(subset=[col])
    if df.empty or pd.isna(val) or val < df[col].min() or val > df[col].max():
        return pd.Series(float("nan"), index=df.columns)
    return df.iloc[(df[col] - val).abs().argmin()]


def _number(value, spec=".0f"):
    return "—" if pd.isna(value) else format(value, spec)


def _hdi(m, lo, hi, dec=0):
    if any(pd.isna(value) for value in (m, lo, hi)):
        return "—"
    return f"{m:.{dec}f} [{lo:.{dec}f}, {hi:.{dec}f}]"


def band_at(df, idxcol, idxval, prefix, dec=0, cov_col=None, cov_min=0.80):
    """Format 'median [ci_lo, ci_hi]' for `prefix` at the row nearest idxval."""
    r = _nearest(df, idxcol, idxval)
    if cov_col is not None and not r.get(cov_col, float("nan")) >= cov_min:
        return "—"
    m = r[f"{prefix}_median"]
    return _hdi(m, r[f"{prefix}_ci_lo"], r[f"{prefix}_ci_hi"], dec)


def plain_at(df, idxcol, idxval, dec=0, cov_min=0.80):
    """Format 'median [ci_lo, ci_hi]' for a single unprefixed series."""
    r = _nearest(df, idxcol, idxval)
    if not r.get("coverage", float("nan")) >= cov_min:
        return "—"
    return _hdi(r["median"], r["ci_lo"], r["ci_hi"], dec)
```

## Method and scope

| Quantity | Model |
| --- | --- |
| DS understood and spoken trajectories, ratios and child variation | VG20 |
| DS signed and total expressive vocabulary | VG15 |
| TD spoken and understood reference trajectories | VG11 and VG12, with study and child effects |
| TD joint reference at matched comprehension | VG21 |

The [model inventory](../models/README.md) records the full set of reporting roles.

Each section states its target. Reference curves set study and child effects to zero; predictive distributions and child-variation summaries include the effects specified in their calculations. Restrict comparisons to the age or vocabulary range supported by both sides.

::: {.callout-important}
TD spoken estimates extend to 30 months and comprehension to 25 months. The joint comparator VG21 spans 8–22 months. A vocabulary level must also be reached within the supported range in enough posterior draws. Tables leave a cell blank where that coverage is below 0.80. Do not read a blank as a zero effect.
:::

## Expected word counts

```{python}
ew_s = pd.read_csv("ds_td_spoken_re_expected_words.csv")
ew_u = pd.read_csv("ds_td_understood_re_expected_words.csv")

ages = [12, 18, 24, 30]
rows = []
for a in ages:
    ru, rs = _nearest(ew_u, "age_months", a), _nearest(ew_s, "age_months", a)
    rows.append({
        "Age (mo)": a,
        "Understood TD": _number(ru['TD_median'], ".0f"),
        "Understood DS": _number(ru['DS_median'], ".0f"),
        "Understood ×": _number(ru['ratio_median'], ".1f"),
        "Spoken TD": _number(rs['TD_median'], ".0f"),
        "Spoken DS": _number(rs['DS_median'], ".0f"),
        "Spoken ×": _number(rs['ratio_median'], ".0f"),
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Age (mo)")
```

These tables and figures compare expected counts on the 810-item reference scale. Read the difference, ratio and uncertainty together. A large ratio near zero can correspond to a small difference in words. These are fitted reference curves, not observed counts for every child.

## Ages at a vocabulary level

```{python}
ad_s = pd.read_csv("ds_td_spoken_re_attainment_delay.csv")
ad_u = pd.read_csv("ds_td_understood_re_attainment_delay.csv")
def _opt(name):
    try:
        return pd.read_csv(name)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
adw_s, adw_u = _opt("ds_td_spoken_re_attainment_delay_weighted.csv"), _opt("ds_td_understood_re_attainment_delay_weighted.csv")

levels = [10, 50, 100, 200, 300]
rows = []
for v in levels:
    row = {
        "Level v (words)": v,
        "Understood delay (mo)": plain_at(ad_u, "words", v, dec=0),
        "Spoken delay (mo)": plain_at(ad_s, "words", v, dec=0),
    }
    if adw_u is not None and adw_s is not None:
        row["Understood, weighted child"] = plain_at(adw_u, "words", v, dec=0)
        row["Spoken, weighted child"] = plain_at(adw_s, "words", v, dec=0)
    rows.append(row)
pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Level v (words)")
```

The attainment difference $D(v)$ is the DS reference curve's crossing age for level $v$ minus the TD reference curve's crossing age. It is not the delay experienced by every child. The weighted-child columns account for the studies represented at each age. Differences between these summaries show how the chosen study reference affects the comparison. A constant $D(v)$ would be consistent with a simple time shift; a changing difference would not.

![Attainment delay D(v), understood](ds_td_understood_re_attainment_delay.png){#fig-ad-u .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![Attainment delay D(v), spoken](ds_td_spoken_re_attainment_delay.png){#fig-ad-s .lightbox fig-align="left"}

### Peak learning-rate age

```{python}
pk = pd.read_csv("ds_td_peak_growth_age.csv").set_index("outcome")
rows = []
for outcome in ("understood", "spoken"):
    r = pk.loc[outcome]
    rows.append({
        "Outcome": outcome,
        "DS peak (mo)": f"{r['peak_age_DS_median']:.0f} "
                        f"[{r['peak_age_DS_ci_lo']:.0f}, {r['peak_age_DS_ci_hi']:.0f}]",
        "DS censored": _number(r['peak_age_DS_boundary_frac'], ".0%"),
        "TD peak (mo)": f"{r['peak_age_TD_median']:.0f} "
                        f"[{r['peak_age_TD_ci_lo']:.0f}, {r['peak_age_TD_ci_hi']:.0f}]",
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Outcome")
```

Peak learning-rate age locates the fastest increase on the fitted curve within the search grid. It requires evidence about the curve's shape, not just its level.

::: {.callout-warning title="Peaks at a search boundary"}
A maximum at the edge of a search grid does not locate a developmental peak. Inspect the fraction of draws with boundary maxima and the permitted reporting range. A numerical peak beyond that range relies on extrapolation and must not be presented as an observed milestone.
:::

## Expressive-specific delay

The following summaries ask whether the population contrast differs between spoken and understood counts. They use different comparisons and should not be read interchangeably.

### At a matched vocabulary size

```{python}
xd = pd.read_csv("ds_td_expressive_delay.csv")
rows = []
for N in [50]:
    r = _nearest(xd, "words", N)
    val = band_at(xd, "words", N, "dexp", dec=1, cov_col="dexp_coverage")
    rows.append({
        "Vocabulary N (words)": N,
        "Δ_exp (extra months to say)": val,
        "P(Δ_exp > 0)": _number(r['dexp_p_gt0'], ".2f") if val != "—" else "—",
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Vocabulary N (words)")
```

$\Delta_{exp}(N)$ subtracts the understood attainment difference from the spoken attainment difference at the same count $N$. Only levels reached by both outcomes in both groups within support can be compared. This difference of curve-crossing ages does not track how long a particular child takes to say the same words they understood earlier.

![Attainment delay: comprehension (blue) vs production (green)](ds_td_expressive_attainment_delay.png){#fig-dexp-attain .lightbox fig-align="left"}

### At a fixed age

```{python}
ca = pd.read_csv("ds_td_expressive_equivalent_age.csv")
rows = []
for a in [24, 36]:
    r = _nearest(ca, "age_months", a)
    val = band_at(ca, "age_months", a, "dexpAge", dec=1, cov_col="dexpAge_coverage")
    rows.append({
        "DS age (mo)": a,
        "Extra expressive delay (mo)": val,
        "P(> 0)": _number(r['dexpAge_p_gt0'], ".2f") if val != "—" else "—",
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("DS age (mo)")
```

At a selected DS age, each expected count is mapped to the age at which the TD reference curve reaches that count. Subtracting the two equivalent ages compares spoken and understood development under those curve mappings. It does not estimate a child's general developmental age.

![DS developmental-equivalent TD age](ds_td_expressive_equivalent_age.png){#fig-cea .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![Receptive vs expressive delay, and the extra expressive gap](ds_td_expressive_delay_by_age.png){#fig-cea-delay .lightbox fig-align="left"}

### Comprehension-matched production ratio

```{python}
qu = pd.read_csv("ds_td_comprehension_q_at_U.csv")
try:
    qo = pd.read_csv("ds_td_comprehension_q_observed.csv")
except FileNotFoundError:
    qo = None
try:
    quw = pd.read_csv("ds_td_comprehension_q_at_U_weighted.csv")
except FileNotFoundError:
    quw = None

def _observed(pop, N):
    if qo is None:
        return "—"
    hit = qo[(qo["population"] == pop) & (qo["words"] == N)]
    if hit.empty:
        return "—"
    r = hit.iloc[0]
    return f"{r['median']:.2f} ({r['q25']:.2f}–{r['q75']:.2f}), n={int(r['children'])}"

rows = []
for N in [50, 100, 150, 200, 300]:
    r = _nearest(qu, "words", N)
    val = band_at(qu, "words", N, "dq", dec=2, cov_col="dq_coverage")
    rows.append({
        "Understood N (words)": N,
        "Curve q TD": band_at(qu, "words", N, "q_TD", dec=2, cov_col="dq_coverage"),
        "Curve q DS": band_at(qu, "words", N, "q_DS", dec=2, cov_col="dq_coverage"),
        "Curve Δq (TD−DS)": val,
        "P(Δq>0)": _number(r['dq_p_gt0'], ".2f") if val != "—" else "—",
        "Weighted child q TD": "—" if quw is None else band_at(quw, "words", N, "q_TD", dec=2, cov_col="dq_coverage"),
        "Weighted child q DS": "—" if quw is None else band_at(quw, "words", N, "q_DS", dec=2, cov_col="dq_coverage"),
        "Children TD: observed q": _observed("TD", N),
        "Children DS: observed q": _observed("DS", N),
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Understood N (words)")
```

The curve columns show the production ratio at the age when each group's reference comprehension curve reaches $N$. They do not estimate $E[q_i\mid U_i=N]$ across individual children. The weighted-child columns change the study reference, while the children columns describe observed administrations near that count. Those administrations can differ between populations in age, study and item composition. Agreement or disagreement between the curves therefore cannot, on its own, establish equality or a deficit among children matched on comprehension.

![Population production ratio at matched comprehension q(U=N)](ds_td_comprehension_q_at_U.png){#fig-qatu .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![Spoken-fraction gap at matched comprehension](ds_td_comprehension_dq.png){#fig-dq .lightbox fig-align="left"}

## Comparison with a reference percentile

```{python}
bp = pd.read_csv("ds_td_below_td_p10.csv")
rows = []
for a in [12, 16, 20, 24, 28]:
    rows.append({
        "Age (mo)": a,
        "Spoken": band_at(bp, "age_months", a, "spoken", dec=2, cov_col="spoken_coverage"),
        "Understood": band_at(bp, "age_months", a, "understood", dec=2, cov_col="understood_coverage"),
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Age (mo)")
```

This is the predicted fraction of DS counts at or below the TD 10th-percentile count at the same age. It compares fitted distributions within their shared age range. The 10th percentile is a reference for this comparison, not a clinical threshold or a norm established for the DS population.

The distributions include new-child effects and count noise at the reference sex and zero study effect. Speech is drawn conditional on simulated comprehension. Each of up to 2,000 paired posterior draws uses 4,096 simulated children per population. These estimates have Monte Carlo error. At a fixed threshold the fraction's simulation standard error is at most 0.8 percentage points; estimating the TD threshold adds uncertainty. Discrete ties can put more than 10% of TD counts at or below that percentile. Check stability with larger simulation sizes before interpreting a small difference.

![Fraction of DS below TD 10th centile, spoken](ds_td_below_td_p10_spoken.png){#fig-bp-s .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![Fraction of DS below TD 10th centile, understood](ds_td_below_td_p10_understood.png){#fig-bp-u .lightbox fig-align="left"}

## Residual count variation

The models separate persistent child differences from variation between assessments. Both contribute to the distribution of observed counts.

- The child-effect scale $\tau$ describes persistent variation on the model's logit scale. It is not the total-spread comparison adopted for reporting below.
- The concentration $\kappa$ describes residual count variation after the model's age, study and child terms. Larger concentration means less residual variation at a fixed mean and denominator.

VG11 and VG12 express child and residual variation through a shared variance budget. Their data and priors determine how that budget is divided. Reading either component alone can hide uncertainty about the division.

The residual count standard deviation $\sigma_Y$ is measured in words. The overdispersion factor $\varphi=(\kappa+n)/(\kappa+1)$ compares variance with a Binomial at the same mean and denominator. It removes the explicit mean term from that formula, but the fitted concentration can still depend on age and model structure. Neither quantity alone measures total variation between children.

For spoken counts, the DS calculation matches the variance of the marginal spoken count to a Beta-Binomial on the full inventory. Using VG20's conditional $\kappa_s$ directly would compare a concentration defined on understood words with VG11's concentration defined on the full inventory. Spoken comparisons made before the 2026-09-02 correction used that incompatible calculation and are superseded.

```{python}
ds_s = pd.read_csv("ds_td_spoken_re_dispersion.csv")
ds_u = pd.read_csv("ds_td_understood_re_dispersion.csv")
rows = []
for a in [8, 12, 18, 24]:
    rs, ru = _nearest(ds_s, "age_months", a), _nearest(ds_u, "age_months", a)
    rows.append({
        "Age (mo)": a,
        "Spoken σ_Y TD": _number(rs['sdY_TD_median'], ".0f"),
        "Spoken σ_Y DS": _number(rs['sdY_DS_median'], ".0f"),
        "Spoken φ TD/DS": _number(rs['phi_ratio_median'], ".2f"),
        "Understood σ_Y TD": _number(ru['sdY_TD_median'], ".0f"),
        "Understood σ_Y DS": _number(ru['sdY_DS_median'], ".0f"),
        "Understood φ TD/DS": _number(ru['phi_ratio_median'], ".2f"),
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Age (mo)")
```

Read the current tables for the size and direction of each contrast.

Counts near zero or a checklist ceiling can have small absolute spread even when children differ considerably in the model's latent effects. A small standard deviation in words should not be treated as evidence that the children are otherwise alike.

![Residual count standard deviation in words, spoken](ds_td_spoken_re_spread.png){#fig-sd-s .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![Residual overdispersion φ (study + subject REs), spoken](ds_td_spoken_re_overdispersion.png){#fig-phi-s .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![Residual count standard deviation in words, understood](ds_td_understood_re_spread.png){#fig-sd-u .lightbox fig-align="left"}

## Total variation in observed counts {#sec-between-child}

The adopted comparison is the standard deviation, in words, of one assessment for a new child. It combines persistent child differences with variation between assessments, while holding the study effect at zero. The posterior interval describes uncertainty about that standard deviation. It is distinct from an interval containing a stated proportion of children's counts.

The same-age comparison includes differences in expected vocabulary level. The same-level comparison instead evaluates each population's spread at the age when its reference curve reaches the selected count. That second comparison is still between modelled trajectories, not between observed children matched on a score.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from pathlib import Path

for _outcome in ("understood", "spoken"):
    for _suffix, _axis, _label in (
        ("total_spread", "age_months", "at matched age"),
        ("total_spread_at_level", "words", "at matched vocabulary level"),
    ):
        print(f"### Words {_outcome}, {_label}\n")
        _path = Path(f"ds_td_{_outcome}_re_{_suffix}.csv")
        if not _path.exists():
            print("Pending. Regenerate the comparison tables from validated fits.\n")
            continue
        _spread = pd.read_csv(_path)
        _rows = []
        _values = [12, 18, 24, 30] if _axis == "age_months" else [10, 50, 100, 200, 300]
        for _value in _values:
            _rows.append({
                "Age (months)" if _axis == "age_months" else "Words": _value,
                "DS SD (words)": band_at(_spread, _axis, _value, "sd_DS", cov_col="sd_DS_coverage"),
                "TD SD (words)": band_at(_spread, _axis, _value, "sd_TD", cov_col="sd_TD_coverage"),
                "Difference (TD minus DS)": band_at(
                    _spread, _axis, _value, "dsd", cov_col="dsd_coverage"
                ),
            })
        print(pd.DataFrame(_rows).to_markdown(index=False))
        print()
```

These tables replace the earlier headline comparison of child-intercept scales alone. That division between persistent and residual variation was difficult to identify, particularly in the typically developing models. The total is not automatically unaffected by the division or by the priors. It needs its own recovery and sensitivity checks. See the [2026-09-14 decision](../../notes/202609141600-total-spread-estimand.md) and [recovery guide](../runbooks/parameter-recovery.md).

Use current, converged recovery runs to assess these quantities. Missing recovery output is a missing check; it must not be filled with a favourable result from an older fit.

## Sign-inclusive expressive gap

```{python}
si = pd.read_csv("ds_td_sign_inclusive.csv")
rows = []
for a in [16, 20, 24, 30]:
    r = _nearest(si, "age_months", a)
    gap_sp = r["gap_spoken_median"]
    gap_any = r["gap_any_median"]
    gap_indep = r["gap_any_indep_median"]
    narrow = (gap_sp - gap_any) / gap_sp if gap_sp else float("nan")
    narrow_indep = (gap_sp - gap_indep) / gap_sp if gap_sp else float("nan")
    rows.append({
        "Age (mo)": a,
        "Sign credit (words)": band_at(si, "age_months", a, "credit", dec=0),
        "Gap (spoken only)": _number(gap_sp, ".0f"),
        "Gap (with sign)": _number(gap_any, ".0f"),
        "Narrowed by": _number(narrow, ".0%"),
        "…if independence assumed": _number(narrow_indep, ".0%"),
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Age (mo)")
```

This compares DS total expressive vocabulary from VG15, $p_{any}$, with TD spoken vocabulary. The difference from a speech-only comparison measures the additional words counted through signing under the fitted overlap model.

The independence column holds the sign and speech margins fixed and sets their within-word association to independence. If $\psi>1$, overlap exceeds the independence value and the independence calculation overstates the union. If $\psi<1$, the direction reverses. Independence is not a general upper bound on expressive vocabulary.

::: {.callout-warning title="Scope of the signing comparison"}
The comparison stops at 30 months because of TD spoken support. Older DS signing observations can inform the fitted curve, but they do not extend the TD comparison range.

The TD reference contains no sign or gesture outcome. Comparing DS speech-or-sign with TD speech therefore does not measure a total-expressive contrast on both sides. It also cannot establish the effect of teaching signs.
:::

![DS expressive gap to TD: spoken-only vs sign-inclusive](ds_td_sign_inclusive_gap.png){#fig-si-gap .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![DS expressive credit from non-speech modalities](ds_td_sign_inclusive_credit.png){#fig-si-credit .lightbox fig-align="left"}

## Words added by counting signing {#sec-ds-signing}

Within the DS sample, the model can estimate the words added by counting sign as well as speech. This question does not require a TD comparator. Quantities combining signing and comprehension remain subject to the comprehension reporting cap.

```{python}
sp = pd.read_csv("ds_signing_profile.csv")
rows = []
for a in [18, 24, 30, 36, 48, 60, 72]:
    r = _nearest(sp, "age_months", a)
    rows.append({
        "Age (mo)": a,
        "Spoken": _number(r['spoken_median'], ".0f"),
        "Any modality": _number(r['any_median'], ".0f"),
        "× spoken alone": band_at(sp, "age_months", a, "uplift", dec=2),
        "Sign-only words": _number(r['sign_only_median'], ".0f"),
        "Share sign-only": band_at(sp, "age_months", a, "sign_only_share", dec=2),
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Age (mo)")
```

Read the absolute sign-only count beside the ratio of total expressive to spoken counts. That ratio can be large when speech is close to zero.

The milestone table distinguishes the peak in sign-only counts from crossings in the shares expressed through each modality.

```{python}
ms = pd.read_csv("ds_signing_milestones.csv").set_index("quantity")
labels = {
    "sign_only_peak_age": "Sign-only vocabulary peaks (mo)",
    "sign_only_peak_words": "…at how many words",
    "sign_only_share_below_half_age": "Sign-only falls below half of expressive vocabulary (mo)",
    "speech_only_overtakes_sign_only_age": "Speech-only overtakes sign-only (mo)",
}
pd.DataFrame([
    {"Milestone": lab,
     "Estimate": _hdi(ms.loc[k, "median"], ms.loc[k, "ci_lo"], ms.loc[k, "ci_hi"], 1),
     "Draws reaching it": f"{ms.loc[k, 'draws_reaching']:.0%}",
     **({"Draws censored": f"{ms.loc[k, 'draws_censored']:.0%}"}
        if "draws_censored" in ms.columns else {})}
    for k, lab in labels.items()
]).set_index("Milestone")
```

The `Draws reaching it` column records how often a crossing occurs inside the grid. A state already true at the youngest age is not an observed early crossing, and an edge maximum does not locate a peak. Where some draws do not cross, any crossing-age summary is conditional on the draws that do. Read it with the crossing probability and reporting limits.

Counts and shares can peak at different ages. The sign-only count is the understood count multiplied by the sign-only share, so the count can still rise while that share falls. Inspect both before describing a decline in signing.

![How DS expressive vocabulary is expressed](ds_signing_composition.png){#fig-ds-sign-comp .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![Signed share and spoken share across age](ds_signing_share.png){#fig-ds-sign-share .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![What counting sign adds to a child's own expressive vocabulary](ds_signing_uplift.png){#fig-ds-sign-uplift .lightbox fig-align="left"}

::: {.callout-important title="Early signing and later speech"}
The [exploratory longitudinal analysis](../../notes/202608160930-early-signing-and-later-speech.md) examined whether earlier signing predicted later speech after adjustment for earlier speech and comprehension. Its dated regression estimates are separate from the parameters of the registered models below.

These associations are not causal effects of teaching signs. Reasons for sign instruction, shared child characteristics and reporting practices can affect them. The available data do not establish the net direction of those biases.

The project distinguishes these questions:

| Question | Quantity | Model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Do children with persistently larger signed shares also have larger spoken shares? | $\rho_{sign\,q}$ | VG24 |
| Within understood words, are words signed and spoken together? | $\psi$ | VG15 and its descendants |
| Does previous-wave signing help predict a later spoken share under the lag definition? | $\beta_{sign\,lag}$ | VG25 |


Read the current role and validation status in the model inventory. A fitted exploratory model is not automatically a source for published estimates, and these three quantities can differ in direction without contradiction.
:::

## Limits on interpretation

The contrasts describe the fitted research samples and depend on their age coverage, measurement choices and model assumptions. They are not population norms or estimates of an intervention effect. Read each comparison with its interval, support and validation record.
